sections.h2: What is Prince George's County, Maryland, and why does its geography matter for a tax bill?
sections.html:
Prince George's County sits on the eastern side of Washington, D.C., and covers about 499 square miles, of which 483 are land. The Patuxent River forms its eastern edge, and only South County touches the Potomac.

Residents and planners talk about five informal regions: North County, Central County, the Rural Tier, the Inner Beltway and South County. U.S. Route 50 is the broad line between north and south. The county seat is Upper Marlboro, and the county was created in 1696 from parts of Charles and Calvert counties.

Geography shows up on the bill in two ways. A house inside an incorporated city, such as Bowie, carries a municipal tax and gets a reduced county rate. A house in unincorporated land pays the county rate in full. Anyone selling should check which one applies before reading a bill.

sections.h2: Who lives and works in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 967,201 people in the county, and the 2025 estimate is 970,374, which makes it the second most populous county in Maryland after Montgomery. The county has had a charter form of government since 1970, with nine council districts plus two at-large seats.

Federal employment shapes the local economy more than most counties. The figures below are 2021 employer counts reported on the county's Wikipedia entry.

For a seller, this means many owners have jobs tied to federal posts and transfers. A reassignment can force a sale on a short clock, which is one reason owners here look for a quick closing.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail connect the county's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The county has 15 Washington Metro stations, and four of them are line ends: Greenbelt, New Carrollton, Largo and Branch Avenue. MARC commuter trains add five Camden Line stops and three Penn Line stops.

  • 28 miles of the Capital Beltway (I-495) run through the county.
  • An 11.5-mile stretch of the Baltimore-Washington Parkway lies inside its borders.
  • The Intercounty Connector opened in 2012.
  • The Purple Line is described as slated to open in 2027.

Distance to a Metro or MARC station is one of the first things a buyer checks, so it also affects how fast a house sells on the open market.

sections.h2: When is the Prince George's County property tax bill due?
sections.html:
The county issues bills every July, and full payment is due September 30. Late payments pick up interest and a penalty, and missing a bill does not excuse the owner.

Owner-occupied homes with a bill marked Principal Residence can pay in two equal parts, the first by September 30 and the second by December 31. Maryland lets local governments add a service charge of up to 1.65% to the second half, according to the state assessments department.

The county's Tax Facts guide gives the late charge as 1.67% per month. The tax year runs July 1 to June 30. Treat that figure as a reason to pay on time rather than a number to plan around.

sections.h2: What rates make up a Prince George's County bill?
sections.html:
A bill is built from several separate rates, each stated per $100 of assessed value. The county's Tax Facts guide lists these fiscal 2026 rates.

ChargeRate per $100 of assessed value
County$1.0000 (reduced in incorporated areas)
State$0.1120
M-NCPPC (Park and Planning)$0.2940
Washington Suburban Transit Commission$0.0260
Stormwater and flood control$0.0540 (Area 1), $0.0120 (Area 2)

The county's own formula is simple: divide the assessment by 100, multiply by the rate, then add any charges. The guide also gives a constant yield rate of $0.9591 for tax year 2026 and a certified unincorporated assessable base of $86.5 billion.

Extra charges can appear on the same bill. Front Foot Benefit covers sewer or water pipes laid in the street (WSSC, 301-206-8032). Solid Waste Service pays for trash and waste programs (Department of the Environment, 301-952-7630). A tax lien charge appears when taxes or fines are in arrears.

sections.h2: How does a reassessment change what an owner pays?
sections.html:
The State Department of Assessments and Taxation sets values, and it reassesses each property every three years. The January 1, 2026 cycle raised residential values in Prince George's County by 10.3% compared with January 1, 2023, and notices went out on December 30, 2025.

Increases are phased in evenly over three years, and decreases take full effect in the 2026 tax year. Homestead and Homeowners' credits are also run by the state, and the county's own credits are listed on its Property Tax Credits page.

Disagreements start with the state assessments department, then go to the county Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then to the Maryland Tax Court. For a dwelling, the appeal board must hold a hearing within 120 days after receiving the request, unless the owner asks for a delay.

sections.h2: Where and how do owners pay in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
Treasury Customer Service at 301-952-4030 handles questions, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The counter is in the Wayne K. Curry Administration Building, 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo.

  • Online through the Tax Inquiry site: $1.50 for an e-check, $3.95 for a Visa debit card, 2.45% for other cards.
  • By phone at 855-516-1830, with added fees.
  • By mail to P.O. Box 37050, New York, NY 10087, with the bill stub.
  • In person at the Largo counter, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Cash is not accepted.
  • A 24-hour walk-up slot at the front entrance takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks, and a drive-up drop box opens at the end of September and December.

Email questions go to tax_inquiry@co.pg.md.us. When a house is being sold, the title company usually pays the bill from proceeds, so the seller only needs the current account balance.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
Real property taxes still unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the county's annual tax sale. That sale turns a late bill into a lien held by a third party, so it is a real deadline.

Owners behind on taxes often find that a conventional listing is difficult, because lenders and title companies need the balance cleared at closing. A cash buyer can sometimes pay the arrears at settlement out of the price. Ask the Treasury Division for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does a seller pay when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Maryland charges transfer and recordation taxes on a sale, and the rates differ by county. A 2026 staff table at the Maryland General Assembly lists Prince George's County at a 1.4% transfer tax and a recordation tax of $2.75 per $500 of consideration, both unchanged from fiscal 2022 through fiscal 2027. The City of Baltimore's finance office lists the state transfer tax as a separate 0.5% of consideration, which applies on top of the local rate.

Which side pays, and how the split is written, is set in the contract of sale. Confirm the exact amounts with the title company, since municipal and state add-ons differ by deal.

sections.h2: What local rules affect a Prince George's County house before it sells?
sections.html:
The county's Office of Homeland Security code compliance staff enforce housing, zoning and rental rules. Inspectors act on complaints or cleanup sweeps and issue a Notice of Violation, a Civil Citation or both, with a deadline to fix the problem.

  • Report a violation by calling 311 inside the county or 301-883-4748 outside it, Monday to Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
  • A single-family rental needs a county license, valid for two years, unless the city or town licenses it instead. Bowie is among the municipalities the county does not license.
  • A license is refused when an inspector finds life-safety violations, including unpermitted construction or an illegal conversion.
  • Landlords who use a pre- or post-settlement occupancy agreement between buyer and seller are exempt from the license requirement.

A house with open citations or unpermitted work can lose bids, so a seller who cannot fix them in time may prefer an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What must a Prince George's County seller disclose?
sections.html:
A seller of a one- to four-unit home must give the buyer a disclosure or a disclaimer statement on or before signing the contract, under Maryland Real Property Code section 10-702. The disclaimer form says the home is sold as-is, apart from known latent defects.

Several sales are exempt, including bank sales after foreclosure, sheriff and tax sales, and transfers by fiduciaries in estates and trusts. A buyer who did not get the statement in time can rescind within five days after receiving it, and the right cannot be waived in the contract.

faqs.q: When is Prince George's County property tax due?
faqs.a: Full payment is due September 30, and bills go out each July. Owner-occupied homes marked Principal Residence can split it into September 30 and December 31 installments.

faqs.q: Where is the Prince George's County Treasury Division?
faqs.a: The customer counter is at 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo, MD 20774, open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. Call 301-952-4030 for help.

faqs.q: Can I pay Prince George's County property tax with cash?
faqs.a: No, the county says cash is not accepted at its counter. It takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks in person, plus cards and e-checks online with fees.

faqs.q: When does the Prince George's County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the annual tax sale. Contact Treasury before then for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: What is the Prince George's County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: A 2026 General Assembly staff table lists 1.4% for the county, with a $2.75 recordation rate per $500. The state adds its own 0.5% transfer tax, so confirm totals with the title company.

faqs.q: Who sets my assessment in Prince George's County?
faqs.a: The Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation does. Reassessment happens every three years, and the January 1, 2026 cycle raised residential values by 10.3%.

faqs.q: Does Bowie get its rental license from the county?
faqs.a: No. The county says Bowie is among the municipalities it does not license, so landlords apply with the city.
